clue.text: Item brought through customs-it causes problems

indicators.note: the words it causes are giving problems, so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of luggage at the border is said to be the source of all the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' is the anagram signal: rearrange IT CAUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage carried past the customs desk is typically a case packed with clothes.

clue.text: King flanked by one pawn and knight in position affording some security?

indicators.note: the chess pieces go inside the word for position

parts.note: a slot is a place or position

indicators.note: something flanked by others has them on each side

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess king guarded by a pawn and knight is in a fairly safe spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanked by' puts K between I P and N; 'in' puts IPKN inside SLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot that tightens when pulled gives a fastening, offering a measure of safety.

clue.text: Show tense child turning up, infiltrating into court

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so this piece goes within the others

parts.note: into gives in

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an elf is a small child, often mischievous

explanation.surface: A nervous child sneaks into a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses ELF to FLE, which is 'infiltrating' IN + CT. 'tense' is grammatical, not nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing a verb's ending marks past or present, so to inflect is how grammar displays tense.

clue.text: About to start endless part song

indicators.note: to start places this piece at the beginning of the answer

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A singer is about to begin a seemingly never-ending part song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ROLE to ROL, with CA 'to start'.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive hymn sung at Christmas is a kind of song.

clue.text: Impose conformity on collapse and disaster

indicators.note: a collapse breaks things apart, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A building collapses and calamity follows; new regulations are imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' is the anagram signal for AND DISASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To make everything follow one set pattern or norm is to enforce uniformity.

clue.text: Sweet is accepted by unassertive type

indicators.note: something accepted by a person is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a timid, retiring person is called a mouse
is contracts to 's, giving S

explanation.surface: A dessert is happily taken on by a shy, retiring person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts S (from 'is', as in it's) inside MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert is a classic sweet course.

clue.text: Who'd give choir a rest, I fancy?

definitions.text: Who'd give choir a rest, I fancy?

indicators.note: fancy signals a rearrangement of the letters, with the I taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who could spare the singers a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle CHOIR A REST and remove I, as 'fancy' with 'I' says. The whole clue is the definition too: the players take over while the singers rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of instrumentalists can play a passage while the singers sit silent.

clue.text: Likely to turn out as intended, like permed, peroxided hair?

definitions.text: Likely to turn out as intended
definitions.meaning: a barometer reading meaning settled good weather ahead, so things look promising
permed hair is set and peroxided hair is blonde, or fair

explanation.surface: Bleached, curled hair suggests things will go according to plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer's settled-weather mark, and literally hair that is styled and blonde.

clue.text: Opening used by those pulling strings getting into Oxford

definitions.text: Opening used by those pulling strings getting into Oxford

parts.words: Opening used by those pulling strings getting into Oxford
parts.note: string pulling suggests influence for a place at the university, but the Oxford is a laced shoe and the strings are laces threaded through holes

explanation.surface: Someone using connections gains a place at Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reinforced hole in a shoe takes the lace.

clue.text: "Casual" is popular in the case of a man, endlessly SO0

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
for can mean regarding or as concerns, like in the case of

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A garment called casual is fashionable for a fellow, says a style note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the E off MALE to leave MAL. The stray 'SO0' at the end is a misread in the paper feed, probably of the letter count, and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal clothes or manners are relaxed and easygoing, the same sense as casual.

clue.text: Woman running around crypt, oddly, to get trimmer

indicators.note: running around something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a woman is referred to as she

indicators.note: oddly means taking the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A lady dashes about a burial vault in search of a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes CYT from crypt, and 'running around' puts SHE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-bladed tool for cutting grass trims a meadow, so it is a kind of trimmer.

clue.text: Sad note struck by neon light originally installed in Malaysian capital

indicators.note: something installed in a place is put inside it

parts.note: KL is the usual short form of Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mournful sound accompanies a neon lamp being fitted up in Kuala Lumpur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives L from light; NE and L are 'installed in' KL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tolled slowly for a death or funeral sounds a mournful tone.

clue.text: Stir created about record causing regret

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the record
to stir is to mix up, so the letters of created are rearranged

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A commotion was caused over a disc, which people came to rue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' rearranges CREATED, and 'about' wraps those letters round EP.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate something is to deplore it or express disapproval, an old sense close to regret.

clue.text: Quiet old German taken ill having consumed fruit

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: something taken ill is out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A silent elderly German became sick after eating fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken ill' rearranges GERMAN as MEGRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A round red fruit full of juicy seeds.

clue.text: Driver with a little craft?

parts.note: the driver is not a motorist but an engine that drives, clamped to the back of a small boat

explanation.surface: A motorist who is a bit crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachable engine fitted to the stern of a dinghy propels the boat.

clue.text: He'll help you to get back to work

definitions.text: He'll help you to get back to work

parts.words: He'll help you to get back to work
parts.note: help to return to employment is the surface, but the back is the spine, put right by manipulation

explanation.surface: An employment adviser promises to get you back in a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who manipulates bones and joints treats bad spines.

clue.text: Governor in Spain keeps cat in animal compound

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the outer piece holds the cat inside

parts.note: governor is slang for father, pa
a tom is a male cat
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A Spanish provincial governor keeps a cat in a zoo enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts TOM inside PA + IN + E. 'Governor' is the old slang for father, and 'compound' is a chemical, not an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance produced by decaying flesh, once blamed for food poisoning, is a chemical from animal matter.

clue.text: MP in marginal facing challenge?

parts.note: a member of parliament holds a seat, so is sitting, and in a marginal seat is easy to hit

explanation.surface: A politician with a slim majority faces a contest at the next election.
explanation.walkthrough: A marginal is a constituency won by a narrow margin; its sitting MP is vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy mark that cannot dodge is a sitting duck, and the incumbent MP literally sits.

clue.text: Humorist in South Germany shows panache

indicators.note: the humorist goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A comedian in southern Germany displays great style.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG goes 'in' S + GER.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut with confident flair is to display style boldly.

clue.text: Forbidding one to approach monarch is relatively grubby

indicators.note: to approach is to come up next to, so the monarch follows on

parts.note: forbidding means stern or grim
the Roman numeral for one is I
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Being barred from going near the king is rather a dirty business.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: dirtier than something else.

clue.text: Leak in space capsule ultimately fixed

indicators.note: something fixed is repaired or rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order
ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A space capsule has a leak that is finally repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges SPACE to ESCAP; 'ultimately' adds E from capsule.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas or water getting out of a container is an outflow, like a leak.

clue.text: Innocent typically held by soldiers in South American TV programme

indicators.note: the built piece is placed inside the abbreviation for South American
something held by another piece sits inside it

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
Innocent is a name taken by several popes, so a typical Innocent is a pope

explanation.surface: A naive person is held captive by troops in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' is not a word for naive here but the papal name. 'held by' puts A POPE inside OR, and 'in' puts that inside SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running domestic drama on television, first sponsored by soap makers.

clue.text: Refractory governess?

parts.note: refractory reads as bending light rather than stubborn

explanation.surface: A stubborn nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass block bends light passing through it, and Wilde's play gives its governess that surname.

clue.text: One question in exercise leads to resentment

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the word for exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single question in a gym lesson causes bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: I + QU go 'in' PE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of pique is wounded pride and irritation.

clue.text: Fellow in a West African country losing a dog

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the built word
the fellow goes inside the run of letters

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A man in Ghana mislays a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes 'in' A + GHANA to make AFGHANA, which then is 'losing' the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-haired hound bred in the Afghan mountains is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Welshman who in France entertains irish for drink

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh man's name

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Welshman who is in France plays host to an Irishman for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' puts IR inside QUI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum cocktail with lime juice and sugar is a mixed drink.

clue.text: Crude paintings possibly found in east, happily with central section removed

indicators.note: something found in another is sitting inside it
removing the central section leaves only the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: Coarse artwork turns up in the Orient, cheerfully cut in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with central section removed' leaves HY from happily; ART is 'found in' E + HY.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and vulgar, the same sense as crude.

clue.text: Go through Act clause by clause?

definitions.text: Go through Act clause by clause?

parts.words: Go through Act clause by clause?
parts.note: the Act looks like a parliamentary statute, but it is an act of a play run through line by line by actors

explanation.surface: Legislators examine a statute section by section.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise a scene by going over each line before the performance.
